methodology.preprocessing: spaCy tokenizer, lowercase alphabetic tokens, English plus Spanish/Indonesian/Portuguese/French/German function-word stoplists and corpus boilerplate stopwords. All records retained; no language translation, lemmatization or silent abstract imputation. Language-specific content words can still form multilingual topics.
methodology.features: Shared 1–2 gram vocabulary; min_df=12, max_df=0.65, max_features=6000. NMF: sublinear TF-IDF; LDA: raw counts.
methodology.coherence: Mean document-level NPMI over all 45 pairs of top 10 terms per topic, measured on held-out 20% documents. Unseen pairs score -1. Higher is better; range [-1,1]. Vocabulary is corpus-wide, so this is descriptive held-out topic evaluation rather than a leakage-free prediction benchmark.
methodology.diversity: Distinct top-10 terms / (10 × topic count), evaluated on training-fit topics.
methodology.stability: Two seeds (42 and 73) on the same 80% training subset, optimally matched by Hungarian assignment of cosine similarity. Seed stability only, not bootstrap robustness.
methodology.interpretability: Lexical distinctiveness proxy: mean fraction of distinct leading words in top 10 terms. Not human-rated interpretability. Inspect labels and representative papers for qualitative assessment.
methodology.trends: Mean normalized topic weight per year, using titles plus available abstracts. Shaded 95% normal intervals reflect sample variability, not model uncertainty. Abstract-only sensitivity also reported. Full-corpus counts are separate unsampled OpenAlex metadata; no volume extrapolation from equal quotas.
methodology.gaps: NMF normalized memberships >=0.15 in abstract-bearing records; both margins >=100; observed below independence baseline. Score = deficit × balanced margins × log(1+smaller margin)/log(1+eligible corpus) × sqrt(cosine topic-term affinity). Similarity is a thematic relevance proxy, not proof of a meaningful intersection. Normalized mixtures impose compositional dependence, so the independence baseline is not a statistical significance test. Threshold and title-only sensitivities are saved. No validated novelty claim.
